newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament to repeat vote on Ciller charge.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament to repeat vote on Ciller charge.

text.p: The Turkish parliament's executive body on Wednesday called for a repeat of a vote on whether to set up a new inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller that could send her to the Supreme Court on corruption charges.

"The voting will be renewed," speaker of parliament Mustafa Kalemli told reporters after a meeting of the executive body, which had investigated challenges against the validity of the initial vote last month.
No date was set for the new vote.
At the initial vote last month, deputies voted against investigating charges of corruption at the state-run tourism company TURBAN which could have lead to an investigation of Ciller's activities.

The Turkish opposition has said two or three government MPs were counted as having voted for Ciller despite not being in attendance at the ballot, at which MPs were initially announced to have voted 247 to 242 against an investigation.
It also said one ballot against Ciller was found on the floor of the debating hall after the result was declared.
The vote could have caused a rift in the government if coalition partner Islamist Welfare Party MPs had swayed it against Ciller.
Earlier last month a 15-member commission voted against an investigation of Ciller's substantial personal wealth for signs of ill-gotten gains during her three years as prime minister, from 1993.

It was the third corruption probe against Ciller, who joined a coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last June -- something she had vowed she would never do until the corruption allegations emerged.

A commission last November rejected a bid to send Ciller to the Supreme Court over allegations she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies. Ciller was cleared earlier of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company.
